messages:
samir (cust): Hey team — after we moved traffic to use AWS PrivateLink to reach Redwood, our production calls are intermittently failing with TLS handshake errors and occasional 502s. It looks like DNS resolves to the VPC endpoint IP but some requests still go out via our NAT and then return with a different src port. Any ideas?

maya (support): sorry to hear — can you paste a minimal repro (curl + verbose) and any tcpdump / flow logs? also which region & vpce type?

samir (cust): region=us-west-2, interface VPCE to our provider (aws service via NLB). repro:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/resource \n  --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.3.12.45
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/resource\n*   Trying 10.3.12.45...\n* TCP_NODELAY set\n* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.3.12.45) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate verify failed\n* Closing connection 0
```

We also grabbed a short tcpdump on the customer ENI and see SYN followed by RST after server sends cert. Flow logs show connections from our private IP -> NATGW -> internet IP for the service intermittently, even though DNS points to VPCE.

kevin (infra): couple quick checks: 1) confirm the VPCE is configured with "Enable Private DNS" for the service domain (otherwise clients may still resolve public IPs depending on resolver cache). 2) Check your route table for the subnet of the client — there should be no 0.0.0.0/0 route that forces traffic to NATGW before the kernel chooses local ENI. 3) Verify Security Groups / NACLs allow ephemeral ports back to the client.

maya (support): also suspicious: TLS handshake failing while connected to the VPCE IP often points to SNI / cert mismatch or an intermediate TLS terminator (proxy/NLB) rewriting SNI or presenting a different cert. Do you have an egress proxy or transparent TLS proxy?

samir (cust): we do have an egress proxy in front of some subnets (squid+mitm). but we thought VPCE connections use the interface and avoid EGRESS path. tcpdump shows sometimes traffic leaves the subnet to NATGW (10.0.0.1) before hitting the interface IP. Not consistent.

kevin (infra): that explains intermittent behavior. Likely root causes to investigate: 
- DNS caching: some hosts still resolving public CNAME -> public NLB IP (TTL) so flows go to NAT.
- Route precedence: if the kernel's resolver returns both IPv4 and ENI addresses, a transient route could prefer NAT path. Check the output of `ip route get 10.3.12.45` from the instance.
- Egress proxy rewriting SNI or doing TLS interception when traffic goes via NATGW/internet. That would cause cert mismatch and handshake fail.

maya (support): repro steps to collect for escalation: 
1) run `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` from affected host(s) and paste results.
2) run `ip route get 10.3.12.45` and `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.3.12.45 https://api.redwood.example.com/resource` and attach full verbose output.
3) attach a 30s tcpdump on the host filtered to port 443: `sudo tcpdump -i any host 10.3.12.45 and port 443 -w /tmp/vpce.pcap` and a snippet of `sudo tcpdump -nn -r /tmp/vpce.pcap | head -n 50`.
4) VPC Flow logs for the subnet / ENI for the timeframe showing whether traffic egressed to NATGW.

eng-oncall-bot: If you want us to escalate, include the above and we can open an eng-runtime ticket. For quick mitigation: 
- Force clients to use the VPCE IP with OS-level `/etc/hosts` entry or `--resolve` for curl to bypass DNS until TTLs expire. 
- If you must use public path temporarily, ensure your egress proxy trusts Redwood CA or allow-list the service to avoid MITM.

samir (cust): thanks — dig shows sometimes the host returns the public NLB IP and sometimes the VPCE IP (TTL 30s). `ip route get` shows pref route to ENI when VPCE ip, but when resolver returns public ip it goes to NATGW. We'll collect the captures and post. For mitigation we'll push /etc/hosts to the cluster while we investigate.

maya (support): perfect — once you post captures we'll triage and optionally escalate. If tcpdump shows SNI mismatch we can ask eng-runtime to check our NLB cert bindings for the service and confirm we aren't serving multiple certs that could confuse MITM proxies. :thumbsup:

kevin (infra): one more note — if you have a shared resolver (eg. forwarder) that resolves external name to public IP even from inside the VPC, enable the VPC DNS private-hosted-zone or use AmazonProvidedDNS (169.254.169.253) for consistent responses.

samir (cust): upload incoming. attaching small pcap and dig outputs now. Appreciate the quick help, will update after we try hosts file push.

maya (support): got it — triaging now. If we confirm NAT path + MITM repro we will escalate and propose a short maintenance window to flip to a direct private route or add a service CIDR allowlist on your egress proxy.
